question: How long is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
answer_en:
The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the insurer [C137]. Important conditions and exceptions include:
- If you enhance the Sum Insured, the waiting period applies afresh to the extent of the sum insured increase [C137].
- If you are continuously covered without any break based on IRDAI portability norms, the waiting period is reduced to the extent of your prior coverage [C137].
- Coverage after the expiry of 36 months is subject to the pre-existing disease being declared at the time of application and accepted by the insurer [C137].

question: Is cataract surgery covered and after how long?
answer_en: Yes, cataract surgery is covered under the policy [C72], but it is subject to a waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage after the inception of the first policy [C138]. Additionally, expenses incurred for cataract treatment are subject to specific limits per eye and per policy period depending on your Sum Insured [C72].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease / procedure waiting period

question: Is there a limit on how much is paid for cataract treatment?
answer_en: Yes, expenses incurred on the treatment of cataract are subject to specific limits per eye and per Policy Period, depending on your Sum Insured [C72]. Additionally, treatment of cataract is subject to a waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage from the date of inception of the first policy, unless the claim arises due to an accident [C138].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease / procedure waiting period

question: Can I claim for an illness in the first month after buying the policy?
answer_en: No, expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date are excluded [C140]. However, this does not apply to claims arising due to an accident, provided they are covered [C140], or if the Insured Person has continuous coverage for more than twelve months [C140].

question: For how many days before hospitalisation are medical expenses covered?
answer_en: Medical expenses incurred before hospitalization are covered for a period not exceeding 60 days prior to the date of hospitalization [C76][C39]. This applies to the disease, illness, or injury sustained, provided there is an admissible claim for hospitalization under the policy and the expenses are for the same condition for which the hospitalization was required [C76][C39].

question: How many days of post-hospitalisation expenses are covered?
answer_en: Post-hospitalisation medical expenses are covered for a period of 90 days from the date of discharge from the hospital [C77]. This applies to expenses for consultant fees, diagnostic charges, medicines, and drugs recommended by the hospital or medical practitioner, following an admissible hospitalization claim for the same ailment [C77]. Additionally, reimbursement claims for post-hospitalisation must be filed within 15 days after the completion of these 90 days [C177].

question: How much does the policy pay for a road ambulance?
answer_en: Subject to an admissible hospitalization claim, the policy pays for road ambulance expenses up to Rs. 750/- per hospitalization and up to Rs. 1,500/- per Policy Period [C78]. This is payable for transportation by private ambulance service for medical reasons to a hospital, from one hospital to another for better treatment, or from the hospital to the place of residence in the same city if certified by a medical practitioner [C78].

question: Are organ donor expenses covered, and is there a limit?
answer_en: Organ donor expenses for organ transplantation where the insured person is the recipient are payable, provided the claim for transplantation is payable and subject to the availability of the Sum Insured [C83]. However, donor screening expenses and post-donation complications of the donor are not payable [C83]. This cover is subject to a limit of 10% of the Sum Insured or Rupees One lakh, whichever is less [C83].

citations.label: Clause 11 - Organ Donor Expenses for organ

question: How soon must I inform the insurer after an emergency hospitalisation?
answer_en: In case of emergency hospitalization, you must inform the insurer within 24 hours of the date and time of hospitalization [C178][C175].

citations.label: Clause B - Documents for Cashless Treatment

question: What is the deadline to file a reimbursement claim after discharge?
answer_en:
The deadline to file a reimbursement claim depends on the type of expense:

* **Hospitalization, day care, and pre-hospitalization expenses:** The claim must be filed within 15 days from the date of discharge from the hospital [C177].
* **Post-hospitalization expenses:** The claim must be filed within 15 days after the completion of 90 days from the date of discharge from the hospital [C177].

Note that these time limits are conditions precedent to the admission of liability, but the company may examine and relax the time limit depending on the merits of the case [C180].

question: Is cosmetic surgery covered?
answer_en: Cosmetic or plastic surgery and any treatments to change appearance are generally not covered [C145]. However, they are covered if they are for reconstruction following an accident, burn(s), or cancer, or if they are part of a medically necessary treatment to remove a direct and immediate health risk to the insured [C145]. For this medical necessity, it must be certified by the attending medical practitioner [C145].

citations.label: Clause Excl08 - Cosmetic or plastic Surgery

question: What is the free look period?
answer_en: The free look period is a duration of thirty days from the date of receipt of the policy document (whether electronically or otherwise) to review the terms and conditions [C196]. This applies only to new individual health insurance policies with a term of one year or more, and not on renewals, porting, or migrating [C196]. If you are not satisfied with the terms and have not made any claim, you can cancel the policy during this period [C196]. You will receive a refund of the premium paid, minus a deduction for a proportionate risk premium for the cover period and any expenses incurred by the insurer for a medical examination and stamp duty charges [C196].

question: How many times can the sum insured be restored in a policy year?
answer_en: The Automatic Restoration of the Sum Insured is available 3 times during the Policy Period [C88]. Each restoration operates at 100% and will occur immediately upon the exhaustion of the Limit of Coverage and only after the exhaustion of any earlier restoration [C88]. This benefit is applicable for specific coverages (II.1, II.2, II.3, II.4, II.6, II.7, II.8, II.9, II.11, II.13, and II.19) and is only available for Sum Insured options of Rs.3,00,000/- and above [C88][C89].

citations.label: Clause 15 - Automatic Restoration of Sum Insured

question: Is knee replacement surgery covered from day one?
answer_en: No, knee replacement surgery (Arthroplasty / Joint Replacement) is generally not covered from day one unless it is caused by an accident [C138]. Expenses related to treatments for diseases related to bones and joints, including joint replacement, are excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy [C138].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease / procedure waiting period

question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
answer_en:
The standard waiting period for pre-existing diseases (PED) is 36 months of continuous coverage from the inception of the first policy with the insurer, unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule [C123]. 

Important conditions and exceptions:
* **Modifications:** You may be able to modify the PED waiting period to 24 months or 12 months if the optional cover for PED waiting period modification is selected at policy inception [C114].
* **Sum Insured Enhancement:** If the sum insured is increased, the waiting period applies afresh to the extent of the increase [C123].
* **Portability:** If you are continuously covered without a break under IRDAI portability norms, the waiting period is reduced by the extent of your prior coverage [C123].
* **Declaration:** Coverage after 36 months requires the disease to have been declared at application and accepted by the insurer [C123].

question: Is cataract surgery covered and after how long?
answer_en: Yes, cataract surgery is covered under the policy [C125]. However, expenses related to its treatment are subject to a specified disease/procedure waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy [C124]. This waiting period does not apply to claims arising due to an accident [C124].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period

question: When will knee replacement surgery be covered?
answer_en:
Knee replacement surgery is covered after a specified disease/procedure waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the company [C124][C126]. 

Important conditions and exceptions:
- This waiting period does not apply to claims arising due to an Accident [C124].
- If the sum insured is enhanced, the waiting period applies afresh to the extent of the sum insured increase [C124].
- If you are continuously covered without any break as defined under IRDAI portability norms, the waiting period will be reduced to the extent of prior coverage [C124].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified Disease/Procedure waiting period

question: Is there a room rent limit?
answer_en:
Yes, there is a room rent limit, which is 'At Actuals' unless otherwise specified in your Policy Schedule [C80]. 

Important conditions regarding room rent:
* **Proportionate Deduction:** If you are admitted in a room that exceeds the category or limit stipulated in your Policy Schedule, the reimbursement or payment of room rent charges and all associated medical expenses will be made in the same proportion as the admissible rate per day bears to the actual rate per day [C82]. This proportionate deduction does not apply if the hospital does not use differential billing for associated medical expenses based on room rent [C82].
* **Optional Modifications:** You can modify your room rent category through optional covers (such as the Optima Lite plan covering up to 1% of the base sum insured per day, or Optima Select options covering a Single Private Room or Shared Room) [C115][C116].

question: How soon must I notify the insurer of an emergency hospitalisation?
answer_en: For an emergency hospitalization, you must send notice with full particulars to the company within 24 hours from the date of emergency hospitalization, or before the insured person’s discharge from the hospital, whichever is earlier [C179].

question: How early should I inform the insurer before a planned hospitalisation?
answer_en: For a planned hospitalisation or when deciding to avail treatment under Home Health Care, you should inform the insurer at least 48 hours prior to admission in the hospital [C179].

question: Within how many days must I submit documents for a reimbursement claim?
answer_en:
The time limit to submit documents for a reimbursement claim depends on the type of claim [C184]:
- For Hospitalization, Day Care Treatment, or Pre-Hospitalization Expenses: Within 30 days of the date of discharge from the Hospital [C184].
- For Post-Hospitalization Expenses: Within 15 days from the completion of post-hospitalization treatment [C184].
Note that any delay in submission may be condoned on merit if the delay is proved to be for reasons beyond the control of the Insured Person [C187].

question: How much cumulative bonus do I get on renewal?
answer_en: On renewal of the policy without a break, a sum equal to 10% (unless otherwise specified in the policy schedule) of the Base Sum Insured of the expiring policy is provided as Cumulative Bonus (CB) irrespective of any claims, up to a maximum of 100% [C89][C196]. For the ‘Optima Select’ plan, the cumulative bonus is 25% of the Base Sum Insured up to 100% [C119][C196]. CB is available only if the policy is renewed or premium is paid within the Grace Period and if the cover is specified to be applicable in the Policy Schedule [C90].

citations.label: Clause 1.8 - Cumulative Bonus (CB) [Applicable to ‘Optima Suraksha’, ‘Optima Lite’ and ‘Optima

question: Does the policy restore the sum insured after a claim?
answer_en:
Yes, the policy restores the sum insured through the Automatic Restore Benefit [C99]. 

- The company instantly adds 100% of the Base Sum Insured if there is an admissible claim during the Policy Year that partially or completely exhausts the Sum Insured [C99].
- It is applied only once during the Policy Year, unless 'Unlimited Times' is specified in the Policy Schedule [C100].
- The restored amount can only be used for subsequent claims during the remainder of the Policy Year, and only for claims admissible under Base Coverage (Section B.1.) and Protect Benefit (Section B.2.3) [C100].
- Unutilized restored Sum Insured cannot be carried forward to subsequent Policy Years [C100].

citations.label: C100 - Specific Conditions applicable to Automatic Restore Benefit

question: What is the free look period?
answer_en: The free look period is thirty days from the date of receipt of the policy document [C153]. It applies only to new individual health insurance policies and not to renewals, porting, or migrating [C153]. During this period, you can review the terms and conditions and return the policy if it is not acceptable, provided no claim has been made [C153]. Depending on the circumstances, you are entitled to a refund of the premium paid minus medical examination expenses and stamp duty, a deduction for proportionate risk premium, or a proportionate premium commensurate with the coverage period [C153].

question: Are childbirth and maternity expenses covered in the base policy?
answer_en: No, childbirth and maternity expenses are not covered under the base policy [C142]. Medical treatment expenses traceable to childbirth (including complicated deliveries and caesarean sections incurred during hospitalization) and expenses towards miscarriage or lawful medical termination of pregnancy are excluded, except for ectopic pregnancies [C142]. However, maternity expenses are covered under the optional 'Parenthood' plan chart after a waiting period of 2 years [C206].

question: Is plastic surgery to improve appearance covered?
answer_en: Expenses for cosmetic or plastic surgery or any treatment to change appearance are generally excluded, unless it is for reconstruction following an Accident, Burn(s) or Cancer, or as part of a Medically Necessary Treatment to remove a direct and immediate health risk to the insured [C132]. For this medical necessity, certification by the attending Medical Practitioner is required [C132]. Additionally, plastic surgery is covered up to the sum insured according to the plan chart [C195] and when necessitated due to Injury [C81].

citations.label: Clause Excl08 - Cosmetic or plastic Surgery

question: Is Ayurvedic treatment covered?
answer_en: Yes, Ayurvedic treatment is covered under the policy. The company will indemnify medical expenses incurred by the insured person for Inpatient Care under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy systems during each policy year up to the sub-limit specified in the policy schedule, in any AYUSH hospital [C85]. AYUSH treatment refers to medical and/or hospitalisation treatments given under these systems [C54].

question: How long do I wait before pre-existing diseases are covered?
answer_en: Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease and its direct complications are excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy [C102]. If you increase the Sum Insured, the waiting period applies afresh to the increased amount [C102]. If you have continuous coverage without a break under portability norms, the waiting period is reduced by your prior coverage [C102]. Coverage after 36 months also requires that the disease was declared at application and accepted [C102]. You can also choose to reduce or completely remove the Pre-Existing Disease waiting time [C100].

question: Is cataract surgery covered and after how long?
answer_en: Yes, cataract surgery is covered under the policy [C103]. However, expenses related to its treatment are excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy [C103]. This waiting period can be reduced if you have prior continuous coverage without any break under portability norms [C103].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease/procedure waiting period

question: When is knee replacement covered?
answer_en: Expenses related to joint replacement are excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy [C103]. This waiting period does not apply to claims arising due to an Accident (covered from day 1) or Cancer [C103]. If the condition falls under the waiting period for pre-existing diseases, the longer waiting period applies [C103]. If you enhance the sum insured, the exclusion applies afresh to the extent of the increase [C103].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease/procedure waiting period

question: Does the 24-month specific disease waiting period apply to cancer treatment?
answer_en: No, the 24-month specific disease waiting period does not apply to cancer treatment [C103]. Cancer is covered after a 30-day waiting period, or from day 1 if arising due to an accident [C103].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Specified disease/procedure waiting period

question: How many days before and after hospitalisation are expenses covered?
answer_en: Expenses incurred on consultations, medicines, physiotherapy, and diagnostic tests are covered for 60 days before the date of admission and 180 days after the date of discharge, provided they are related to the condition for which the hospitalization claim is paid [C53].

citations.label: Clause 4.3 - Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)

question: Is there a restriction on the hospital room I can choose?
answer_en: The policy does not limit your choice of hospital room, and you can choose the room you like, but you should choose judiciously to protect your Sum Insured [C49]. You can choose between a Single Private Room and a Sharing Room according to your lifestyle, and once chosen, this cannot be changed [C101]. However, if you opt for a hospital room higher than your eligible room category specified in your Policy Schedule, a pro-rated portion of total Associated Medical Expenses will be paid based on the formula: (Eligible Room Rent limit / Room Rent actually incurred) * total Associated Medical Expenses [C151].

citations.label: Clause 4.2.1 - We will pay the expenses incurred by you…

question: Is road ambulance covered, and up to how much?
answer_en: Road ambulance is covered up to the Base Sum Insured [C46]. However, this will only be paid if the claim for hospitalization is also paid by the insurer, and you must always use a registered ambulance provider [C48].

question: What does ReAssure Forever do?
answer_en: ReAssure "Forever" provides an unlimited Sum Insured [C62]. The first paid claim in the life of the policy triggers ReAssure "Forever", and once triggered, it stays for life as long as the policy is renewed without a break [C62]. The maximum amount ReAssure "Forever" pays for any single claim is up to the Base Sum Insured [C63]. A claim is considered if it is paid under Expenses in reaching a Hospital, Expenses during Hospitalization, Expenses before and after hospitalization, Home Care / Domiciliary Treatment, or Organ Donor [C63]. Additionally, expenses in reaching a hospital and expenses before and after hospitalization for the 1st ever hospitalization will be treated as the 1st claim itself [C63].

question: What happens to the sum insured I don't use in a year?
answer_en: Under the Booster+ benefit, your unutilized Base Sum Insured carries forward so you don't lose what you don't use [C70]. It can accumulate up to a maximum of 3, 5, or 10 times the Base Sum Insured, depending on the plan you have chosen [C70].

question: What is the free look period?
answer_en: The Free Look Period applies to new individual health insurance policies and not to renewals or policy porting/migrating [C126]. The insured is allowed a free look period of 15 days (30 days for policies with a term of 3 years, if sold through distance marketing) from the date of receipt of the policy document to review the terms and conditions and return the policy if not acceptable [C126]. If no claim has been made during this period, the insured is entitled to a refund of the premium paid, less any expenses incurred by the Company for medical examinations [C126].

question: Is LASIK surgery to remove my glasses covered?
answer_en:
LASIK surgery to remove glasses is covered under certain conditions:
* Expenses related to the treatment for the correction of eye sight due to refractive error are only covered if the refractive error is **7.5 dioptres or more** [C114].
* Less than 7.5 dioptres means a power of eye either greater than 7.5 dioptre for hypermetropia (far sightedness) or less than 7.5 dioptre for myopia (near sightedness) [C114].

question: Within how many days must I submit reimbursement claim documents?
answer_en: All claim documents must be submitted within 30 days from discharge [C151]. If there is any delay in submission, you must provide the reasons in writing, and the company will condone such delay on merits for reasons beyond your control [C151].

question: What is the waiting period for pre-existing diseases?
answer_en:
Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing disease (PED) and its direct complications are excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the insurer [C120].

Important conditions and exceptions:
- By choosing the Optional Benefit for PED Wait Period Modification, this 36-month waiting period can be modified to a specific time period mentioned in the Policy Schedule [C97].
- If the sum insured is enhanced, the exclusion applies afresh to the extent of the increase [C120].
- If the insured person is continuously covered without a break under portability norms, the waiting period is reduced to the extent of prior coverage [C120].
- Coverage after 36 months is subject to the disease being declared at the time of application and accepted by the insurer [C120].

question: Is cataract surgery covered and after how long?
answer_en: Yes, cataract surgery is covered under the policy [C121]. However, expenses related to its treatment are excluded until the expiry of a 24-month waiting period of continuous coverage from the date of inception of the first policy with the company [C121]. This waiting period applies even if the condition is contracted after taking the policy or declared and accepted without a specific exclusion [C121]. If you have continuous coverage without a break under portability norms, the waiting period is reduced by your prior coverage [C121].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Named Ailment Waiting Period

question: Is knee replacement covered and when?
answer_en: Joint replacement surgery (which includes knee replacement) is covered under the policy after a waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage from the date of inception of the first policy with the company [C121]. However, this waiting period does not apply to claims arising due to an accident [C121]. If the sum insured is enhanced, the waiting period applies afresh to the increased amount [C121]. If you are continuously covered without a break as per IRDAI portability norms, the waiting period will be reduced by your prior coverage [C121].

citations.label: Clause Excl02 - Named Ailment Waiting Period

question: Is there any room rent limit?
answer_en:
Yes, under the Base Benefits for Hospitalization Expenses, the eligible Room Rent or Room Category applicable for the Insured Person is 'No limit', meaning there is no separate restriction on room charges incurred during hospitalization [C86]. Similarly, there is no limit on ICU charges under the base benefits [C86], and there are no ICU charges limits under the Room Rent Modification optional benefit either [C96]. 

However, if you opt for the 'Room Rent Modification' optional benefit, your room category is limited to a Single Private AC room or a Twin sharing room as specified in your Policy Schedule [C95]. If you stay in a room with a higher rent or category than your eligible limit, you will have to bear a ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses [C95].

question: For how many days before admission are medical expenses covered?
answer_en: Medical expenses incurred for a period of 60 days immediately prior to the insured person's date of admission to the hospital are covered, provided they are medically necessary, incurred during the policy year, and related to the same illness or injury for which the company has accepted a claim under hospitalization expenses [C84].

question: How long after discharge are post-hospitalisation expenses covered?
answer_en: Post-hospitalisation medical expenses are covered for a period of 180 days immediately after the insured person's date of discharge from the hospital [C84]. Claim documents must be submitted within 30 days after the completion of these 180 days [C84]. These expenses must be medically necessary, related to the same illness or injury for which the hospitalization claim was accepted, and incurred through a reimbursement facility up to the sum insured [C84].

question: How does the cumulative bonus work?
answer_en:
The Cumulative Bonus is an increase or addition in the Sum Insured granted by the insurer without an associated increase in premium [C10]. At the end of each Policy Year, the Company enhances the Sum Insured by 50% flat, on a cumulative basis, for each completed and continuous Policy Year, subject to conditions [C88]:

* **Cap:** The accrued Cumulative Bonus shall not exceed 100% of the Sum Insured available in the expiring Policy or renewed Policy, whichever is lower [C88].
* **Continuity:** It is forfeited if the policy is not continued or renewed on or before the Policy Period End Date or the expiry of the Grace Period, whichever is later [C88]. Claims do not impact its accrual [C88].
* **Changes in Sum Insured:** If the Sum Insured is reduced at renewal, the Cumulative Bonus is reduced in proportion [C89]. If increased, it is calculated on the Sum Insured applicable on the last completed Policy Year [C89].
* **Exclusions:** The 'Unlimited Automatic Recharge' and 'Plus Benefit' amounts are not considered when calculating it [C89].
* **Utilization:** It can be utilized for Base Benefits like 'Hospitalization Expenses' and 'Road Ambulance Cover' [C89].

citations.label: Clause 2.1.8 - Cumulative Bonus mean any increase or

question: Is the sum insured recharged after it is used up?
answer_en:
Yes, if a claim is payable under the policy, the company automatically makes an unlimited automatic recharge of up to the base sum insured in a policy year, which is valid for that policy year only [C90]. However, this is subject to the following conditions:
- The recharge is utilized only after the base sum insured, applicable cumulative bonus, cumulative bonus super (if applicable), and plus benefit (if applicable) are completely exhausted in that policy year [C90].
- A claim is admissible under the recharge only if it is admissible under the 'Hospitalization Expenses' benefit [C90].
- The recharged amount can be used for the same illness as well as different illnesses [C90].
- The sum insured available under this benefit can only be used for 'Hospitalization Expenses' and 'Road Ambulance Cover' [C90].
- All insured persons are eligible to use the recharged amount for any illness or injury pertaining to that policy year [C90].
- Any unutilized recharge cannot be carried forward to any subsequent policy year [C90].

question: How soon must I inform the insurer after an emergency hospitalisation?
answer_en: In case of an emergency hospitalization, you must notify the company either at their call center or in writing immediately, and in any event within 48 hours of the hospitalization commencing or before the insured person's discharge from the hospital [C180].

question: What is the deadline to file a claim after discharge?
answer_en: The deadline to file a claim is within 30 days from the date of discharge from the hospital in case of hospitalization [C179][C177]. For reimbursement facilities, all information and documentation must be submitted within 30 days of the insured person's discharge from the hospital at the policyholder's or insured person's own expense [C177]. However, in case of delayed submission, the company may examine and relax the time limits upon the merits of the case [C177].

question: What is the free look period?
answer_en: The Free Look Period is 30 days from the date of receipt of the policy document to review the terms and conditions and return the policy if not acceptable [C159]. This period applies only to new individual health insurance policies, and not to renewals or when porting or migrating the policy [C159]. If no claim has been made during this period, you are entitled to a refund of the premium paid minus any medical examination expenses and stamp duty charges, or a proportionate risk premium deduction if the risk has commenced, or a proportionate premium commensurate with the coverage if only part of the coverage has commenced [C159].

answer_en: No, this policy does not pay for childbirth expenses. The policy explicitly lists maternity expenses—including medical treatment expenses traceable to childbirth, complicated deliveries, and caesarean sections—as standard exclusions [C139].

question: ముందుగా ఉన్న వ్యాధులకు వేచి ఉండే కాలం ఎంత?
answer_en: For pre-existing diseases (PED), the standard waiting period is 36 months of continuous coverage from the inception date of the first policy with the insurer, unless specified otherwise in the Policy Schedule [C123]. This waiting period can optionally be modified to 24 months or 12 months if such an option is stipulated in the Policy Schedule [C114].
answer: ముందుగా ఉన్న వ్యాధులకు (Pre-Existing Diseases) సాధారణంగా 36 నెలల నిరంతర కవరేజ్ కాలం వేచి ఉండే కాలం (waiting period) ఉంటుంది [C123]. పాలసీ షెడ్యూల్‌లో వేరే విధంగా పేర్కొనకపోతే, మొదటి పాలసీ ప్రారంభ తేదీ నుండి ఇది వర్తిస్తుంది [C123]. పాలసీ షెడ్యూల్‌లో నిర్దేశించినట్లుగా, ఈ వేచి ఉండే కాలాన్ని ఆప్షనల్ కవర్ ద్వారా 24 నెలలకు లేదా 12 నెలలకు తగ్గించుకునే అవకాశం ఉంది [C114].

question: क्या इस पॉलिसी में कमरे के किराए की कोई सीमा है?
answer_en: Under this policy, the eligible Room Rent or Room Category and ICU charges are 'No limit', which means there is no separate restriction on Room Charges or ICU charges incurred towards stay during hospitalization [C86][C96]. However, if the optional benefit 'Room Rent Modification' is opted, the eligible room category is limited to a Single Private AC room or Twin sharing room as specified in the Policy Schedule, and staying in a higher room category will require bearing a proportional amount of associated medical expenses [C95].
answer: इस पॉलिसी के तहत कमरे के किराए (Room Rent) और आईसीयू (ICU) शुल्क के लिए कोई सीमा नहीं है, जिसका अर्थ है कि अस्पताल में भर्ती होने के दौरान कमरे के शुल्क पर कोई अलग प्रतिबंध नहीं है [C86][C96]. हालाँकि, यदि आपने 'रूम रेंट मॉडिफ़िकेशन' (Room Rent Modification) नामक वैकल्पिक लाभ चुना है, तो कमरे का किराया पॉलिसी अनुसूची में निर्दिष्ट सिंगल प्राइवेट एसी रूम (Single Private AC Room) या ट्विन शेयरिंग रूम (Twin Sharing Room) तक सीमित हो सकता है, और यदि आप इससे अधिक महंगा कमरा लेते हैं, तो आपको आनुपातिक चिकित्सा खर्च (pro-rata expenses) उठाने होंगे [C95].

question: రోడ్ అంబులెన్స్ ఖర్చులు ఎంత వరకు చెల్లిస్తారు?
answer_en: Subject to an admissible hospitalization claim, road ambulance expenses up to Rs.750/- per hospitalization and up to Rs.1,500/- per Policy Period are payable for transportation of the Insured Person by private ambulance service to a hospital for medical reasons, from one hospital to another for better treatment, or from the hospital to their residence in the same city if certified by a medical practitioner [C78].
answer:
ఆమోదించదగిన ఆసుపత్రి ఖర్చులకు లోబడి, రోడ్ అంబులెన్స్ ఖర్చులు ఒక్కో ఆసుపత్రిలో చేరడానికి రూ.750/- వరకు మరియు పాలసీ కాలవ్యవధికి రూ.1,500/- వరకు చెల్లించబడతాయి [C78]. ఇది ఈ క్రింది వాటికి వర్తిస్తుంది:
- వైద్య కారణాల రీత్యా ఆసుపత్రికి వెళ్లడానికి ప్రైవేట్ అంబులెన్స్ ద్వారా రోగిని రవాణా చేయడానికి [C78].
- మెరుగైన వైద్య చికిత్స కోసం ఒక ఆసుపత్రి నుండి మరొక ఆసుపత్రికి ప్రైవేట్ అంబులెన్స్ ద్వారా రవాణా చేయడానికి [C78].
- వైద్యుడు అంబులెన్స్ అవసరాన్ని ధృవీకరించినట్లయితే, చికిత్స పొందిన ఆసుపత్రి నుండి వారి నివాస స్థలానికి (అది ఒకే నగరంలో ఉంటే) రవాణా చేయడానికి [C78].

question: Is knee replacement covered and after how long?
answer_en: Yes, joint replacement is covered, but it is subject to a waiting period of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy [C103]. This waiting period does not apply to claims arising due to an accident [C103]. If it falls under the waiting period for a pre-existing disease, the longer of the two waiting periods shall apply [C103].
answer: हाँ, घुटने के प्रतिस्थापन (joint replacement) को कवर किया जाता है, लेकिन इसके लिए पहली पॉलिसी शुरू होने की तारीख से 24 महीने की निरंतर कवरेज पूरी होने तक प्रतीक्षा अवधि (waiting period) होती है [C103]। यह प्रतीक्षा अवधि दुर्घटना के कारण होने वाले दावों पर लागू नहीं होती है [C103]। यदि यह स्थिति पहले से मौजूद बीमारी (Pre-existing Disease) के अंतर्गत आती है, तो दोनों प्रतीक्षा अवधियों में से जो लंबी होगी, वह लागू होगी [C103]।
